prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Mission/scope: Hospital automated medication dispensing and initial medication-return handling cover order intake, pharmacy preparation/verification, and ward access, supporting timely fulfillment while preserving pharmacist oversight, medication traceability, and clinical control.
Elements, actors, aliases, and responsibilities:
• Medication Order Gateway: controlled medication-order entry; communicates order status to authorized hospital systems.
• Clinical Pharmacist: reviews clinical appropriateness, resolves medication questions requiring professional judgment, and produces the Dose Exception Review Slip for orders requiring documented exception review.
• Pharmacy Technician: performs routine preparation within approved procedures; escalates discrepancies to the Clinical Pharmacist.
• Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot (Cinderwake): produces the Priority Refill Tote Tag for eligible refill work; prepares eligible medication against the active order and records handling actions.
• Pharmacy Verification Station (Juniper): supports final verification before medication release for delivery or ward access.
• Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler: maintains monitored storage conditions for medication requiring temperature control.
• East Tube Dispatch Console and West Tube Dispatch Console: controlled routing interfaces for authorized pharmacy deliveries.
• Pneumatic Tube Network: carries compatible deliveries between designated hospital locations under established routing procedures.
• Registered Nurse (Larkspur).
• Charge Nurse: coordinates ward readiness, communicates operational constraints, and supports escalation during dispensing-service disruption.
• Medication Return Kiosk (Tallowmere): controlled recording of medication returns and capture of return details; produces the Return Bin Audit Label for a recorded return transaction.
• Hospital Courier: supports authorized movement of medication and returns when automated routes are unavailable or unsuitable.
• Biomedical Engineer: maintains supported equipment.
• IT Operations Specialist: monitors system connectivity and service availability.
Constraints: Ward medication access remains subject to local authorization, patient-care requirements, and applicable cabinet controls. Returned medication remains segregated from usable stock until disposition is assessed under hospital procedure. No explicit operating modes are defined.

Document units:
S025: The Medication Safety Officer oversees safety concerns, reviews relevant trends, and supports updates to medication handling procedures.
S026: The Medication Order Gateway is called Morrowglass in this concept.
S027: The Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler is called Bluejay in this concept.
S028: The Pharmacy Technician is called Copperfield in this concept.
S029: The Medication Order Gateway accepts medication orders from authorized clinical systems and records their arrival times.
S030: It checks required order fields, patient identifiers, medication codes, quantities, and destination details before routing an order for pharmacy review.
S031: The gateway flags missing data, duplicate submissions, and changes that conflict with the active order record.
S032: The Medication Order Gateway produces the Order Reconciliation Snapshot for documenting detected order discrepancies.
S033: The Pharmacy Verification Station displays queued orders and their validation results for review.
S034: The Clinical Pharmacist evaluates clinical appropriateness, dose limits, allergies, and relevant interactions before approving an order.
S035: The Pharmacy Technician investigates administrative discrepancies and requests clarification through approved clinical channels.
S036: Unresolved discrepancies keep an order from advancing to preparation.
S037: The Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot prepares only orders that have passed the required review and authorization checks.
S038: The Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler maintains refrigerated medications within the facility's approved temperature range.
S039: Continuous sensors record temperature readings and report excursions or loss of monitoring connectivity.
S040: The Pharmacy Technician checks the cooler's status and confirms that refrigerated stock remains within handling limits before use.
S041: The Pharmacy Technician produces the Cold Chain Handoff Card to document custody and handling conditions.
S042: When an excursion occurs, affected stock is segregated pending assessment and disposition by authorized pharmacy staff.
S043: Temperature records are retained with timestamps so reviewers can establish the duration and extent of an excursion.
S044: The Clinical Pharmacist determines whether affected medication remains suitable for dispensing under approved procedures.
S045: The Pharmacy Technician checks packaging, product identity, lot details, and expiry information during routine stock handling.
S046: The Medication Safety Officer reviews patterns of discrepancies and handling events for potential safety concerns.
S047: The Medication Safety Officer produces the Diversion Review Packet when a diversion concern requires documented review.
S048: The Pharmacy Verification Station preserves review decisions and order status changes in an auditable record.
S049: Orders remain unavailable for dispensing until required checks are complete and their status is authorized.
